newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee prices stable despite N.Y. rally.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee prices stable despite N.Y. rally.

text.p: Indonesian local coffee prices generally were little changed on Monday as a rally in New York last Friday had little impact on the local market, where players are closing their books at the end of harvests, traders said.
They said grade four Robusta was around 2,650-2,700 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 2,600-2,700 rupiah a week ago.
The export price fob Lampung was $1,200-$1,210/tonne, up slightly from $1,200 last week.
"Unless there is a major rise in overseas' prices, I don't think local prices will move up very much," one trader said.
Traders said they expected London prices to open a little higher but added that the upside would be limited.
"Vietnam has been active in October/November positions. Its harvests are expected to begin later this month and the peak is expected to come in November," he said.
The trader said Vietnam might be offering its new crop at around $1,170-$1,180/tonne, while its carryover crop was being quoted at $1,210 against $1,270 last week.
"London might probably go $10 higher (when it opens on Monday), but not much beyond that," he said. Another trader said almost three-quarters of Indonesia's production had been sold.
The trader said that of the estimated exportable quantity of 325,000 tonnes, 300,000 tonnes had been sold.
"There's not much beans left, and my estimate is that there will be a carryover of around 25,000-30,000 tonnes," he said.
Another trader said some sellers were attempting to hold back sales in anticipation of better prices, but added that many who wanted to keep cash flow healthy preferred to sell.
"The big players have stocks on their hands but they are not expected to chase prices," he said.
